refined_nucleus: The vascular graft incorporates a machine learning-based predictive model to detect early signs of bacterial colonization and adjust the release of antimicrobial agents accordingly.
new_relationship: The integration of machine learning algorithms with the vascular graft's ceramic layer release mechanism enables real-time monitoring and adjustment of antimicrobial agent release.
new_configuration: The addition of a microelectromechanical systems (MEMS) sensor to monitor bacterial colonization and adjust the ceramic layer's release mechanism.
new_control_rule: The control logic is modified to include a machine learning-based predictive model that adjusts the release of antimicrobial agents based on real-time monitoring of bacterial colonization.
refined_structure: The vascular graft consists of an ePTFE luminal layer, a biodegradable polymer layer, a ceramic-polymer interface layer, a MEMS sensor, and an embedded, porous ceramic layer.
refined_causal_chain: MEMS sensor detection of bacterial colonization
Machine learning-based predictive model adjustment of antimicrobial agent release
Real-time adjustment of ceramic layer release mechanism
addresses_attacks: adversarial attack on the ceramic layer's release mechanism
adversarial attack on the vascular graft's structural integrity
remaining_risks: unintended consequences of machine learning-based predictive model on graft function
